summary: Streaming response stalls mid-generation during TLS session-ticket rotation at edge
description:
Issue summary: Customers report long-running streaming chat sessions (SSE or WebSocket) abruptly stop emitting tokens ~90-150s into generation. No 5xx returned; TCP remains established for some clients, others see silent close. Impact: customer-facing production outages for BrightLeaf Health internal chat assistant causing timeouts and degraded UX.

Observed behavior: stream produces tokens for ~1-2 minutes, then output ceases without final event or error. Client-side metrics show no inbound data but no explicit connection close in many cases. Server-side request handlers show worker still listed as processing until request eventually times out.

Expected behavior: continuous token streaming until generation completes or an explicit error is returned. Keepalive or heartbeat should prevent silent stalls across LB/termination boundaries.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs a long-form chat generation (prompt ~3-4k tokens output expected) using SSE with keepalive disabled on client.
2) Traffic routes through our public edge TLS terminator (configured with session-ticket rotation every 90s in staging of same config as prod).
3) Observe token emission for ~1-2 minutes then silent pause; client receives no final event and does not get 502/504 immediately.
4) Reproduce frequency increases when multiple concurrent long-lived streams flow through same LB instance and when kernel-switch events occur on workers.

[serving-runtime] 2026-03-12T10:23:14Z INFO stream: worker 17 token-streaming (req_id=rb-9a2c) emitted 312 tokens
[serving-runtime] 2026-03-12T10:25:05Z WARN stream: downstream write returned EPIPE for req_id=rb-9a2c (no upstream error)

comments: [2026-03-12] Aisha Kapoor (Support): Customer opened after three separate chat attempts stalled around 90-150s. Provided client-side debug logs and a sample request. Marking P1 due to production outage for core workflow.

[2026-03-12] BrightLeaf Engineer (customer): We see the same behavior from both our web client and an internal server-to-server consumer. Adding verbose TLS and tcpdump output (attached). Willing to route a small percentage of traffic through a diagnostic edge.

[2026-03-12] Miguel Santos (SRE): Investigating. Early hypothesis: TLS session ticket rotation at edge LB coincides with stall window. Asking infra to check LB rotation schedule and if session resumption is attempted mid-stream.

[2026-03-13] Infra (edge team): Confirmed keyset rotation cron runs every 90s in the prod edge pool (non-default tuning from older config). Temporary change: increased rotation interval to 24h for affected edge pool for BrightLeaf routing. Observed reduced reproduction during small pilot.

[2026-03-13] Miguel Santos (SRE): Implemented temporary workaround and requested customer validate. Suggested client-side keepalive comments at 15s and a retry-on-silent-pause backoff. Customer reports immediate reduction in incidents in pilot.
[2026-03-14] Release Lead (Engineering): Hotfix merged to avoid tearing TLS sessions for long-lived streams (PR #242). Planning canary rollout across 3 edge nodes in us-west on 2026-03-15.
[2026-03-14] Aisha Kapoor (Support): Updating ticket with canary schedule. Will coordinate post-rollout verification with BrightLeaf.
investigation_notes: 1) Reproduced locally by simulating TLS session ticket rotation at 90s in a dev edge: SSE stream frequently halts mid-generation when rotation occurs while downstream TCP socket remains open.

2) Root cause hypothesis: session-ticket rotation triggers session rewrap on LB which causes TLS renegotiation or rekey path that some clients treat as `connection change` and stalls application-layer read loop — server continues writing but TLS layer buffers/discards without propagating error to app until write fails or timeout.

3) Additional contributor: a subset of worker kernel-switch events (quantized model fallback) cause temporary stop-the-world GC-like pauses in runtime scheduling which align poorly with rewrap timing, increasing chance of stall.
4) Not all clients are affected: clients using aggressive keepalive heartbeats or reconnect logic do not show user-visible outages. Browser-based SSE without client heartbeat is most impacted.
5) Observed no definitive 5xx from runtime; edge and lb logs show TLS key rotation messages at same timestamps as first silent periods.
resolution: Workaround applied (2026-03-13): increased session-ticket rotation interval for BrightLeaf routed edge pool to 24h and enabled application-level SSE heartbeat comments every 15s for affected customers. Customer validated reduction in incidents in pilot routing.

Code fix (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-config/pull/242): edge-config change prevents mid-stream session rewrap for connections flagged as long-lived (SSE/WebSocket) and defers keyset rotation until connection close or a graceful rehandshake. Merged 2026-03-14.

Runtime patch: serving-runtime v1.3.2 adds explicit application-layer heartbeat emission for SSE endpoints and better handling when TLS layer reports write-side transient rekey events. Canary rollout scheduled 2026-03-15 in us-west, full rollout expected 2026-03-18 after monitoring window.

Follow-ups: update runbook with troubleshooting steps for TLS-session-related streaming stalls, add synthetic long-stream tests in staging that exercise key rotation scenarios, and recommend clients enable simple heartbeat comments or short reconnect logic as best practice.
Post-incident actions: create INT ticket to audit edge key rotation schedules across regions (INT-4513). Ensure documentation of the long-lived connection flag for routing (confluence page updated).
Customer communication: BrightLeaf notified of canary and full rollout schedule and provided recommended client changes. Ticket owner to close after full rollout and 72h stable monitoring.
